title: finding(plugin-detail): `DetailSection`'s collapsible branch never reads `section.showBorder`, so a declared `showBorder: false` keeps its border
body:
Found while implementing objectui#8626 (session `session_01UzHd6hDYatoDn17BuwKxnZ`) and **out of that card's scope**, which is the flat-versus-`section` prop-shape mismatch on the `detail-section` registration. `DetailSection` is that card's declared CONTROL — it stays byte-identical there — so this is recorded rather than repaired on that branch. No assignee, left for triage.

## What was observed, on `origin/main` at `b775500af`

`DetailViewSection.showBorder` is honoured on exactly one of `DetailSection`'s three render branches.

`packages/plugin-detail/src/DetailSection.tsx` ends in three returns:

1. the flat branch — `const isFlat = !section.title && !section.collapsible && section.showBorder === false;` — reads it;
2. the non-collapsible Card branch — `className={cn(section.showBorder === false ? 'border-none shadow-none' : '', className)}` — reads it;
3. the **collapsible** branch — a `Collapsible` wrapping a bare `Card` with no `className` at all — **never reads it**.

So a section authored with both `collapsible: true` and `showBorder: false` keeps its border and shadow. The key is silently dropped, on the one branch where the author asked for two things at once.

## Reproduction

Measured as a failing assertion while writing objectui#8626's pin, through the real `SchemaRenderer` and the real registry:

```tsx
render(
  <SchemaRenderer
    schema={{
      type: 'detail-section',
      title: 'Billing Address',
      collapsible: true,
      showBorder: false,
      fields: [{ name: 'street', label: 'Street' }],
    }}
  />,
);
// container.querySelector('.border-none') === null   -- the border stays
```

The same node with `collapsible: false` renders `border-none shadow-none` as declared. That is the whole difference.

⚠️ That reproduction is only available from an SDUI-authored node once objectui#8626 lands (before it, every `detail-section` node draws an error banner instead). The defect itself is older and independent of it: it is equally reachable today through `DetailView` / `SectionGroup`, which pass `section={...}` to `DetailSection` directly.

## Why it is worth a card

`showBorder` is a **declared** key on three surfaces at once — `DetailViewSection` in `@object-ui/types`, its `DetailViewSectionSchema` Zod mirror, and the `detail-section` registration's `inputs` (so `sdui-parser`'s `validateTree` tells an author it is correct and complete). An author writes it, publishes clean, and gets a border anyway. That is ADR-0049 enforce-or-remove territory: either the collapsible branch honours the declaration, or the declaration is narrowed to say where it applies.

## Not pre-judged

Whether the collapsible branch should carry `border-none shadow-none` on its `Card`, or whether the chrome of a collapsible section is deliberately fixed, is a design question this card does not pick.

## Scope note

Not touched by the objectui#8626 branch. That card registers the `detail-section` tag against a seam adapter that folds the eight declared inputs into the `section` object the component reads; `DetailSection` itself is unchanged there, by design and proven byte-identical. Its pin authors `collapsible: false` on the `showBorder` row for exactly this reason, and says so in place.
